messages:
leo (acme-ops): Hey team — after we switched our Redwood API traffic to the new VPC endpoint in us-east-1 (PrivateLink) we're seeing intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures. Latency also spiked from ~100ms to ~1.2s for some requests. This started right after we created a private hosted zone and attached the endpoint to the prod subnets.

maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this, leo. Can you paste the simplest repro (curl + dig) and any error output? Also what region and whether you used NLB vs ALB in front of the service?

leo (acme-ops): Repro below. Region: us-east-1. We're using an NLB with TLS passthrough to the RedCaps (pods) but the VPCE points at the NLB.

--- dig output ---
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> api.redwood.internal
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer: ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.internal. 60 IN CNAME vpce-0192abcd-abcdef.vpce-svc-1234.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.
vpce-0192abcd-abcdef.vpce-svc-1234.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com. 60 IN A 10.0.5.23

--- curl output ---
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/hello
* About to connect() to 10.0.5.23 port 443 (#0)
* Connected to 10.0.5.23 (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* SSL: certificate subject name (api.redwood.example.com) does not match target host name 'api.redwood.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (api.redwood.example.com) does not match target host name 'api.redwood.internal'

leo (acme-ops): Also intermittently we see: "upstream prematurely closed connection" in the client logs (502).

sre-bot: (automated) Attached NLB health check failure spike at 2026-03-15T12:30Z (see metric id #nlb-hc-342).

maya (support): Two quick hypotheses: 1) split-horizon/private hosted zone resolving to the VPCE IP is correct, but host header/SNI don't match what the backend expects (cert CN mismatch) — causing TLS failures. 2) NLB health checks or security group/NACLs are killing some connections intermittently causing 502s. Can you run an openssl s_client test and a curl with --resolve to compare?

leo (acme-ops): Ran these:
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.redwood.example.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood.example.com
   i:/CN=redwood-internal-ca
---

$ curl --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.23 https://api.redwood.example.com/health -v
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* successfully set certificate verify locations:
* TLS connection established, cipher ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-length: 2

maya (support): That confirms it — when the client uses the internal name (api.redwood.internal) the TLS cert Subject doesn't match, but forcing the public host via --resolve passes. Two paths: either (A) make the private hosted zone record match the SAN/CN used by certs (preferred: issue certs for internal name or use the public name in PHZ) or (B) change the NLB listener to TCP passthrough and let client SNI reach backend exactly as expected.

jake (eng-infra): Quick checks from our side: please share the endpoint's acceptance status and ENI attachments. Also validate Route53 PHZ association is only for the VPCs that should see the VPCE. Common problem: PHZ associated with staging VPCs in another region causing some clients to resolve to wrong endpoint IP (cross-region PHZ leakage). Run:
$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*vpce*" --region us-east-1
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name api.redwood.example.com
And check NLB target-group health details:
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <tg-arn>

natalie (networking): Also double-check security groups on the ENIs attached to the VPCE. I've seen SGs that allow 443 from the VPCE only but block ephemeral ephemeral ports from the NLB -> targets, which results in intermittent connection resets (502). Check NACLs too for deny rules.

leo (acme-ops): Ran the describe-target-health, shows some targets Unhealthy intermittently with reason "TLS handshake timeout" and a couple "connection reset by peer". ENI SG looks like this:
- sg-0a1b2c3d: ingress 443 from sg-vpce-xxx, egress 0.0.0.0/0 restricted to 443 only (we tried to lock egress).

jake (eng-infra): There's the problem — egress restricted to 443 only on the target instances/ENIs can break health checks and backend callbacks (metrics, auth providers) that use other ports/ephemeral ranges. Targets may attempt outbound to internal auth or KMS and get blocked, causing timeouts and unhealthy states. Change egress to allow ephemeral ports and the internal control plane IPs, or use a NAT with proper allowlist.

natalie (networking): Actionable checklist for leo:
- Update ENI/instance egress to allow ephemeral ports (1024-65535) to your internal control-plane IPs and allow NLB health-check IPs.
- Confirm PHZ is scoped only to the prod VPCs and not shared across regions.
- If you need to keep internal name, ensure cert SANs include api.redwood.internal or use TLS passthrough and preserve SNI.
- Verify NACLs don't have DENY rules that affect ephemeral ranges.

leo (acme-ops): We loosened egress to internal control-plane (10.1.0.0/16) and ephemeral ports, and re-associated PHZ only to prod-vpc. After that: health checks stabilized and TLS handshake errors dropped to zero. Latency back to ~120ms median (some cold starts still). Good catch.

maya (support): Great to hear. We'll record this as an escalated root cause: PHZ association + overly restrictive ENI egress + cert/SNI mismatch. I'll attach recommended remediation steps and a short explainer for customers who want PrivateLink + TLS: include cert SAN planning or use TCP passthrough NLB.

leo (acme-ops): One last question — we saw one-off billing shape where some calls were billed as public egress before fix. Any gotchas?

maya (support): If traffic briefly went to internet egress (egress via NAT) while PHZ reconfiguration was in flight, that could cause public egress billing. Check your VPC flow logs and your cloud billing line items for the timeframe 2026-03-15T12:20–12:40Z. We can open a billing ticket if you see unexpected charges.

leo (acme-ops): Will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maya (support): Marking resolved from support side — please ping if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:
